issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Stock.add(String): The UML in the problem statement declares Stock.add(String) with return type void, while both the template and the reference solution define public int add(String ingredient) that returns the updated quantity (or -1 if the ingredient is not found). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended contract: implementing a void version (as in the UML) would diverge from the provided code and the solution's behavior, and expecting an int return is necessary to match the template/solution implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and code. Recommended: update the problem statement UML and any textual description to declare Stock.add(String): int and document that it returns the updated quantity (or -1 when ingredient not found). Alternatively, if the educational intent is to have a void method, change the template and solution implementations to return void and adjust callers/tests accordingly. Prefer updating the UML here because both template and solution already use int.
